# @ddtcorex/maestro-reviewer

The Maestro merge-request review engine and its GitLab CI flow: reviewer and
auditor agents, comment

and finding posting, review history and signals, the
`resolve` job, the reviewer Docker image and t

he CI templates. It needs no DSH
web host, no settings store and no local checkout.

The DSH host side (GitLab webhook intake, project mappings with local
worktrees, the Maestro Review

Settings section, Telegram digests) is the
separate plugin `@ddtcorex/dsh-maestro-review`,
which run

on, Telegram digests) is the
separate plugin `@ddtcorex/dsh-maestro-review`,
which runs this engine.
## What it provides

- **Review engine** (`src/host/engine.ts`, Cordis row `maestro-review-engine`,
service `reviewEngine

`): one review run from an explicit configuration
(GitLab URL, token and bot username, model, agent

timeout, profile) and a
code access mode: `diff` (the GitLab diff only), `clone` (the source cloned

at the head SHA) or `workspace` (a worktree the caller prepares).
- **Forge boundary** (`src/host/fo

rge/`): the engine reaches GitLab only through
`ReviewForge`, implemented in `forge/gitlab/`.
- **Fi

ndings, history and signals**: findings come only through the
`report_review_findings` tool of tool-

only review agents; history and the
running and final MR markers are tracked per MR.
- **Review tool

s** (workspace search, Magento and Hyva scans, query-log stats,
GitLab diff tools) mounted into revi

ew runs, and the bundled
`dsh-native-tools` skill (row `maestro-review-host`).
## CI reviewer (no local checkout)

The same pipeline also runs headless from GitLab CI: a shared reviewer
project (holds secrets and th

e image) serves any number of source projects
through a small bridge job, with no DSH host and no pr

s any number of source projects
through a small bridge job, with no DSH host and no project mapping.

- **Trusted trigger.** The reviewer project forbids pipeline variables, and a
`resolve` job asks Git

Lab which MR triggered it, so a source project can
never change what the reviewer runs or where its

secrets go. The pipeline
file lives in a separate Maintainer-only config project, so every developer

can trigger a review while only Maintainers can change what receives the
keys.
- **Per-project prov

iders.** Each source project can bring its own AI provider
and key (`openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini`,

`openrouter`, `deepseek` presets or
any OpenAI-compatible endpoint), set as reviewer variables scop

ed
`review/<project id>`; a require switch guarantees a paying project never
falls back to the defau

lt key.
- **Per-repository settings.** A `.maestro-review.yml` on the target branch
sets the profile

, extra ignore globs, project rules, the minimum severity
to post, the comment language and the fan-

out thresholds; an MR cannot
change the settings its own review runs with.
- **Safe input.** Secrets

and personal data are redacted before any model
call, and generated, vendored and lock files never

reach the model; large
MRs are reviewed in parallel parts, re-pushes only by their interdiff.
- **MR

commands.** `/maestro explain`, `/maestro fix` (a GitLab suggestion
block), `/maestro rereview [pat

h]` and `/maestro dismiss [CODE]`, answered
by the next review job; a code a project keeps dismissin

g is muted.
- **Optional gate and reports.** `REVIEW_GATE=blocking` fails the review job
while the M

R has an open blocking thread; a Code Quality artifact and a
scheduled periodic report (findings, to

kens, tool calls per project).
- **Quick** runs diff-only (or on a checkout when `REVIEW_PROFILE` na

mes a
framework); **deep** runs once per head SHA on the `maestro-review::deep`
label, cloning the M
R head with a static-only audit.

Step-by-step GitLab setup, the access each user and token needs, every
variable with its scope and f

lags, daily use, and troubleshooting: `docs/ci-reviewer-setup.md`.
Templates live in `templates/`, t
he image in `docker/`.
## Settings

Reads its configuration through the **shared namespaced settings store**
(`~/.dsh/dsh-maestro-config

/settings.json`) via the flat adapter in
`src/host/config-store.ts`, over the embedded store copy `s

rc/host/vendor/store.ts`
(generated from `dsh-maestro-core`, no runtime dependency); machine runtime

state stays in a
package-local sidecar.

## Release

A release ships **two artifacts that must stay in lockstep**: the npm
package and the `ddtcorex/maes

tro-reviewer` Docker image — the image
installs the npm package from the registry rather than copyin

g source, so
tagging a release alone is not enough to ship it to CI users. In short:
bump `package.j

son` + `CHANGELOG.md` + the three image-tag references →
tag `vX.Y.Z` (triggers npm publish + GitHub

Release) → bump
`profiles/reviewer-ci/package.json`'s own pin to match → rebuild and push
the Docke

r image. Full step-by-step checklist, including the pnpm
supply-chain age-gate workaround and how to

live-test a fix in the image
before a full release: see **Release checklist** in `AGENTS.md`.
